title: java / Working with Java projects
content:
## Working with Java projects

There are three things you must understand to work with Java in {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %}:

1. How does {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} handle Workspaces?
2. How does {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} handle Java?
3. How does {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} handle Workspaces that contain Java?

### {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} Workspaces

In {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode %}, a "Workspace" means a collection of one or more filesystem folders (and their children) and all of the {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} configurations that take effect when that "Workspace" is open in {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %}.  There are two kinds of "Workspaces" in {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %}, "folder workspaces" and "multi-root workspaces".

A "folder workspace" is presented by {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} when you open a filesystem folder (directory) in {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %}.

A "multi-root workspace" can refer to multiple folders (directories) from disparate parts of the file system and {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} displays the contents of the folder(s) of the workspace together in the [File Explorer](/docs/editing/getting-started/userinterface.md#basic-layout). To learn more, see [Multi-root Workspaces](/docs/editing/workspaces/multi-root-workspaces.md).

### Java projects in {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %}

In contrast to IDEs such as IntelliJ IDEA, NetBeans, or Eclipse, the concept of a "Java project" is provided entirely by extensions, and is not a core concept in the base {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %}. When working with "Java projects" in {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %}, you must have the necessary extensions installed to work with those project files.

For example, Maven, Eclipse, and Gradle Java projects are supported through [Language Support for Java™ by Red Hat](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=redhat.java), by utilizing [M2Eclipse](https://www.eclipse.org/m2e/), which provides Maven support, and [Buildship](https://github.com/eclipse/buildship), which provides Gradle support through the [Eclipse JDT Language Server](https://github.com/eclipse/eclipse.jdt.ls).

With [Maven for Java](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=vscjava.vscode-maven), you can generate projects from [Maven Archetypes](https://maven.apache.org/guides/introduction/introduction-to-archetypes.html), browse through all the Maven projects within your workspace, and execute Maven goals easily from an embedded explorer. Projects can also be created and managed with the [Project Manager for Java](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=vscjava.vscode-java-dependency) extension.

<video autoplay loop muted playsinline controls title="Using the Java Projects view from the Project Manager for Java extension">
  <source src="images/java/package-viewer.mp4" type="video/mp4">
</video>

{% data variables.product.prodname_vscode %} also supports working with standalone Java files outside of a Java project, described in the [Getting Started with Java](/docs/java/java-tutorial.md) tutorial.

### {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} Workspaces that contain Java projects

Assuming the necessary Java extensions are installed, opening a {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} workspace that contains Java artifacts will cause those extensions to understand those artifacts and present options for working with them.

More details about Java project support can be found in [Java Project Management in {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode %}](/docs/java/java-project.md) and [Java Build Tools](/docs/java/java-build.md).
